Bounder

Bounder uses three d6 for the Dealer and two d20 for the Shooter. The Shooter sets the opening stake and rolls the first d20 to establish a point. The Shooter may double their stake before the Dealer rolls.

Wagers

Other participants can stake on the Shooter’s point, on all three Dealer dice being odd, on all three being even, or on the Dealer rolling three alike. The point bet loses if the Dealer total equals the first d20 result. Odd and even bets pay an amount equal to their stake; a three-alike bet pays three times its stake.

Dealer and Shooter rolls

The Dealer rolls 3d6, then the Shooter rolls the second d20. The Shooter and point bettors win an amount equal to their stake when the two d20 results bracket the Dealer total, with one roll higher and one lower. A matching second d20 loses. If the pair is 1 and 20, only the Shooter doubles their stake gain. The next clockwise eligible participant becomes the Shooter for the next game.

Loaded dice

A Shooter with an item slugged games-loaded-dice may choose either d20 result from their private panel. Without that item, the module rolls the d20 normally.

Source acknowledgement. Bounder originates in Pathfinder #159: All or Nothing, p. 76, as presented by Archives of Nethys.
